sources.title: Adopted decision on the 2026 Kazakhstan visa exemption
sources.publisher: Government of Montenegro, published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: The MFA's public temporary-exemptions page links this adopted DOCX, Decision 11-011/26-1467 of 17 April 2026, published there on 28 April. Article 1 expressly sets the Kazakhstan document, dates and stay; it is not the separate draft with blank adoption fields.

sources.title: Kazakhstan: current Montenegro MFA visa regime
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Montenegro
sources.officialityEvidence: The current destination-authority country page's Vizni režim section expressly states that Kazakh citizens need a visa, identifies consular issuance, and separately states the 1 May–1 October 2026 exemption for up to 30 days with a valid travel document.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Državljani Republike Kazahstan moraju posjedovati vizu za ulazak u Crnu Goru.

sources.title: Visa regulation consolidated through Gazette 108/26
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Montenegro
sources.officialityEvidence: The MFA landing page, published 6 August 2026, links the complete DOCX consolidated through Gazette 108/26. Article 4 is an express visa baseline, Article 7 preserves supporting-document exceptions, and Article 12c addresses future regulation of exemptions by special acts.
sources.supportingExcerpt: na osnovu važeće strane putne isprave u koju je unesena viza.

sources.title: MFA visa procedure and travel-document validity
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Montenegro
sources.officialityEvidence: The current MFA guidance expressly describes personal applications and diplomatic/consular issuance. Only the travel-document and visa-procedure sections are used; its older nationality list is not used against the later consolidated regulation.
sources.supportingExcerpt: A visa is issued by the state administration authority responsible for foreign affairs, through a diplomatic and consular mission.

policies.title: Montenegro: Kazakhstan seasonal waiver through 1 October 2026
policies.summary: The adopted 2026 decision and current Kazakhstan guidance allow entry, transit and stays up to 30 days without a visa with a valid Kazakh travel document from 1 May through 1 October 2026.
conditions: This ordinary-passport visitor policy is limited to the stated seasonal window and requires a valid travel document.
The MFA's general document rule requires issuance within the preceding ten years and validity for at least three months after planned departure, subject to its stated emergency exceptions.
The 30-day limit does not establish a right to continue this seasonal exemption beyond 1 October 2026; work, residence and final admission are separate matters.

allowedStays.label: Up to 30 days during the 1 May–1 October 2026 seasonal waiver
notes: The source gives a seasonal entry, transit and stay window, not an exemption beyond its endpoint.

policies.title: Montenegro: Kazakhstan prior-visa baseline from 2 October 2026
policies.summary: After the specific seasonal exemption ends on 1 October, the MFA's express Kazakhstan visa requirement and the regulation's Article 4 baseline apply to ordinary passport-only visitors. This confirms the existing future override from 2 October 2026.
conditions: The visa is issued through a diplomatic or consular mission. The Kazakhstan page identifies the Bulgarian embassy in Kazakhstan as an alternative where the traveller cannot approach a Montenegro mission; no electronic-issuance route is established.

Article 7 separately allows qualifying holders of valid Schengen, Australian, Japanese, Canadian, New Zealand, Irish, US or UK visas, qualifying residence permits, or APEC business travel cards to use its document-conditioned route for up to 30 days and no longer than the supporting document remains valid. This does not make a Kazakh ordinary passport alone visa-free.

Article 12c prevents exemptions being regulated by special government acts from 31 October 2026, and seasonal exemptions from 1 October. It does not expressly replace the specific Kazakhstan decision's endpoint; this policy preserves the published 1 October endpoint and the existing 2 October baseline.
This baseline does not displace the current seasonal route before 2 October or determine special-passport, work, residence or final admission treatment.

conflicts.explanation: Prospective difference only: visa-free is supported on 22 September and through the specific 1 October endpoint. The explicit normal visa baseline applies from 2 October. The repository already has a matching future override; this batch rechecks its evidence, not a present-day status correction.
